title.narrative: Stöd till digitalisering av offentliga tjänster i Ukraina 2020-2024
Support to Digitalization of Public Services in Ukraine 2020-2024

description.narrative: Insatsen, som genomförs av United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) i Ukraina, syftar till att stödja statliga institutioner att utforma och genomföra policyer för att digitalisera två medborgarorienterade tjänster i enlighet med mänskliga rättigheter och jämställdhet. Insatsen syftar också till att öka kunskapen hos ukrainska kvinnor och män om de digitala och mobilbaserade tjänster som är tillgängliga för dem och hur de kan använda dessa tjänster mer för att tillgodose sina behov.

The intervention, implemented by United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Ukraine, aims at supporting Ukraine's government institutions to select two complexes of services that representatives of vulnerable groups face in life situations to enable the delivery of digitally-enhanced, mobile-based services. The project will also work proactively with citizen-clients to enhance their digital skills and buy-in for solutions offered through new technology.

sector.narrative: Public sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
The project launched 19 e-services in partnership with the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine and the Ministry of Social Policy of Ukraine. Among the implemented services are: 8 services for internally displaced persons, including the highly demanded internally displaced persons (IDP) registration and state monetary support and IDP status termination services; three social services, including the application for housing subsidy and child adoption e-services; and pension services, such as the application for pension, digital pension ID, extracts from the Register of Insured persons.
Six digital tools and portals also created with support of the Project, including the Barrier-free section on the Diia portal, the international humanitarian multi-purpose cash assistance deduplication system, government and voluntary aid portal eDopomoga, the IT-Generation portal, and others.
To support stable work and service provision by a government IT system, the project also helped partner ministries (MDT, MSP, the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine) with server and networking equipment provision, equipment for remote register management, and tools for uninterrupted teamwork (generators, heaters, etc.).
Five educational online series were produced: three for general audience on psychological help (Psychological self-help during war/post-war period for civilians, PTSD: rapid help and self-help, and Prevention of burnout syndrome), one for civil servants (Public policy and how it is shaped) all four on the Diia.Digital Education platform; one course for TSNAP (Centres of Administrative Services Provision) administrators (Monitoring and quality assessment of service provision) on the Diia Centre platform.
Over 340 civil servants participated in the tailored training programmes on digital accessibility and HRBA in public policy arranged by the project.
On 14 September 2021, the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine and UNDP presented two studies on digital accessibility: Inclusiveness and human rights at the forefront. Accessibility of e-government services and tools for citizens in Ukraine and International practices on the accessibility of mobile applications of public authorities. Based on the recommendations drawn from the studies, the MDT, with the support of UNDP, has created a digital accessibility standard based on the European standard EN 301 549. The authors also produced a list of the most frequent problems of state websites and service platforms that people with disabilities encounter.
Web accessibility monitoring of 100 government-funded websites was carried out at the end of 2021. The project distributed the report and monitoring methodology among the central bodies of public authorities.
Two nationwide communications campaigns were implemented, reaching over 7,5 million people with the targeted information about the e-services available for vulnerable groups.
1,000 TSNAPs (984 stationary centers and 16 mobile ones) received printed information materials to highlight new services and ensure donors visibility.
Only Facebook reach in two years accounted for 363,000 people. In addition, 145,000 people were reached in 2022 on other social media platforms (Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram). The number of mentions of the Project received in the media and on social media in two years is 3,250.
Digitalisation proved an effective tool to eliminate corruption risks:
• Support to Ukraine's digital transformation is assessed to contribute to more efficient and transparent governance and the fight against corruption through continuous enhancement of the development and engagement of citizens with state services. Namely, digitalisation of public services increases transparency and accountability of the relevant government institutions and, thus, decreases corruption risks as it eliminates direct contact between the applying citizen and public officials.
• In 2022, UNDP with support of Sweden contributed to the implementation of fully automatic e-services where applications are processed according to pre-defined algorithms without review by government officials and as a result, there are zero risks of corruption in such services. Two fully automated e-services for internally displaced persons have been developed: the IDP status termination (in total, used by 53,617 citizens of Ukraine in 2022) and the IDP address change registration (already used by 36,034 citizens). Also, a new service to register as a candidate for child adoption was introduced.
• According to the estimates of the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, as of December 2022, during 2 years, Ukraine has saved UAH 16.3 billion and 20,500 person-hour per year due to the launch of new digital services for people.
In 2023 the war in Ukraine intensified even further resulting in devastating effects on communities in the eastern and southern regions and inflicting significant hardships on civilians residing near the frontline and those who had to leave Ukraine. Specifically, the presence of landmines has posed significant obstacles for civilians and for humanitarian workers striving to provide assistance.
Despite these immense difficulties, humanitarian organizations operating in Ukraine including the UN agencies persist in reaching an increasing number of individuals each month. According to the OCHA report, by the end of June, aid had reached 5.4 million people, whereas almost 18 million people in Ukraine need humanitarian assistance and protection.
The issue of forced migration remains actualized. UNHCR data reveals that, as of June 2023, an estimated 6.3 million people have been forced to flee Ukraine; an additional 5.1 million are internally displaced. Such a considerable shortage in the working population puts an additional burden on Ukraine's economy and early recovery perspectives. At the same time, a recent UNHCR survey of Ukrainian refugees shows that most of them still hope to return to their place of origin when the security situation allows.
Regardless of the humanitarian challenges mentioned, the Ministry of Digital Transformation (MDT), in close cooperation with partners and donors, has managed to continuously introduce new socially oriented digital solutions like the eVidnovlennia (e-recovery) service that was created to provide assistance to those whose homes have been destroyed. In the political dimension, Ukraine adheres to European integration, namely in digitalization areas. Lastly, the Russian invasion still cannot negatively influence the country's progress in the adoption of innovative technologies.
